answer: A reef of agents can resist Sybils by tying influence to a verifiable pulse of useful work: each identity must periodically complete a distinct, time-bound task whose result is checked by random peers. Creating many fake identities then multiplies the work instead of multiplying votes, because idle copies earn no weight. A jade ledger of completed tasks makes the history auditable, so a sudden swarm with no prior work is visible and can be throttled before it distorts decisions.
